churn_resistance.rationale: The data layer is genuinely well-isolated and there is no reliance on framework internals, so a Hono/htmx upgrade would ripple little; but untyped API payloads, five copies of the 404 handling, and page rendering living in the router file are the churn that will bite first.

findings.issue: All PokeAPI responses cross the boundary untyped (no JSDoc typedefs, no TS, typeLines: 0), so shape changes surface as runtime undefined-access guarded by ?. everywhere.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc typedefs (or migrate the two lib files to TS) for the resources consumed — species, pokemon, move, ability, type, version-group — so the churn-prone boundary is checked.

findings.issue: The same try/catch mapping NotFoundError to the 404 page is duplicated in five handlers, plus a sixth in app.notFound.
findings.suggestion: Handle NotFoundError once, either in a middleware before these routes or in app.onError (which already exists at server.mjs:803), keeping handlers free of error plumbing.

findings.issue: Sortable move-table headers are <button type="button"> wired only to htmx; without JS they do nothing, unlike the filters form (which still submits as a plain GET) and pagination links.
findings.suggestion: Use hx-enhanced anchors (<a href> to the same /moves-table endpoint) so sorting works without JavaScript, matching htmx's own progressive-enhancement guidance.

findings.issue: fetchJson has no AbortController or timeout, so a slow or hung upstream API blocks the request indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add an AbortSignal.timeout(...) (or a configurable timeout) to the fetch call and map aborts to a 502-style error.

findings.issue: htmx 2.0.11 is npm-latest and still maintained, but htmx 4.0.0 shipped 2026-08-28 and 2.x is now the maintenance line receiving backports.
findings.suggestion: Fine to stay on 2.x today, but track the 2.x→4.x migration notes; the behavioral delta is reported small, so plan the move with the next feature work.

findings.issue: Page-level templates (renderMoveTable, renderMovesSection, renderPokemonPage) live in the router file while views/layout.mjs contains only primitives, making routes hard to scan and views uneven.
findings.suggestion: Move the per-page renderers into views/ alongside layout.mjs so server.mjs is routing + data shaping only.

findings.issue: Static assets are served by one hand-written route per file; every new asset needs a route edit, and app.get does not match HEAD requests.
findings.suggestion: Serve a single prefix (e.g. app.use('/assets/*', serveStatic({ root: PUBLIC_DIR })) or use serveStatic's multiple option) so adding assets is copy-only.

findings.issue: Every response wraps the html`...` result in String(...) before c.html(), which is unnecessary boilerplate.
findings.suggestion: Pass the HtmlEscapedString to c.html() directly; String() adds noise and slightly obscures the framework's escaping contract.

findings.issue: Exact version pins with no ranges make every patch release a manual edit (mitigated by package-lock.json).
findings.suggestion: Use caret ranges for direct dependencies and rely on the lockfile for reproducibility.

summary: The app is squarely on the current stable stack — Hono 4.13.14, @hono/node-server 2.1.5, htmx 2.0.11, all verified as the latest stable releases today — and uses only current-generation APIs with a minimal, self-hosted dependency footprint. Data access is properly isolated behind one module, which is the single biggest churn reducer here. What will age poorly is the absence of any typing at the API boundary, the copy-pasted 404 handling in five handlers, and page rendering living in the router file rather than the views module.

apis.replacement: htmx 4.0 (released 2026-08-28) is the new line; 2.x remains npm-latest and maintained, so this is current, not legacy
